memory_candidates.content: In skill-orchestrate's Stage MT-3 lifecycle-cycling loop, eligibility is recomputed from scratch every cycle, so any per-cycle exclusion decision re-fires forever unless it is also recorded in an INVOCATION-SCOPED deferral set on mt_state_file. deferred_self_modifying is the established template: the set is (1) checked in step 2's all-terminal test so a deferred task does not keep the loop alive, (2) subtracted in step 3's eligible_tasks build so the exclusion converges, (3) excluded from step 4's no-eligible circuit-breaker 'stuck tasks' framing, and (4) reported by Stage MT-5 as a category distinct from both completed_tasks and failed_tasks while forcing exit_status='partial'. Any NEW deferral cause must add its own named set rather than reusing deferred_self_modifying, because the operator remedy differs per cause; mirroring all four sites is the whole cost of adding one. This template was reused verbatim to add deferred_deploy_checkpoint/deployed_critical_paths for the inter-cycle redeploy checkpoint.

Before hardening a bash script for automated self-invocation from inside the same repo it modifies, confirm the target sync/write mechanism's actual write mode (truncate-in-place vs. write-temp-then-rename) rather than assuming. Neovim's vim.fn.writefile() truncates in place ('An existing file is overwritten, if possible' per its own docs) with no atomic rename. A bash script executed as `bash path/to/script.sh` reads the file incrementally by byte offset; if that same script is the deploy target and TARGET defaults to the current repo, the deploy will overwrite the very file bash is mid-execution-reading, corrupting subsequent reads. The fix: wrap the entire executable body in a single function (e.g. main()) defined in full before any of it runs, invoked as the file's last physical line with nothing after it -- this forces bash to fully parse the function body before execution starts, so a later mid-execution overwrite of the on-disk file cannot corrupt already-parsed control flow. Verified live: the pre-fix script crashed with a bash parse error when self-invoked against its own repo; the post-fix script completed cleanly in the identical scenario.
